story.title: Inflation erased the income gain.
story.dek: New federal figures show inflation absorbed the gain in after-tax income.
story.script: A new report shows inflation swallowed Americans' income gains. The Bureau of Economic Analysis said Wednesday that after-tax income rose in August. Prices rose too, leaving buying power flat. Annual inflation was three point four percent, above the Fed's two percent goal. The next test: can income start outpacing prices? That's what gives households more room to breathe.
story.reviewMethod: Editorial accuracy review against BEA release 26-43 and the Federal Reserve definition of its longer-run PCE inflation goal. Aggregate estimates, not every household's experience.
story.editorialNote: BEA released these August estimates on September 30, 2026, with its annual update. Annual headline PCE inflation was 3.4%; the Federal Reserve goal is 2% over the longer run. After-tax income rose 0.3% in current dollars and was unchanged after inflation; real spending rose 0.6%. No comparison uses unrevised July figures. The closing is a question, not a forecast.
story.visualDisclosure: Original Bearing explanatory graphics drawn from public-domain federal data, with source credits. No documentary footage or third-party photographs. Locally synthesized AI narration; original synthesized music.

review.accuracy: Every quantitative claim checked against BEA release 26-43; 2% longer-run PCE goal checked against the Federal Reserve FAQ. No claim about each person's pay, no CPI substitution, no market prediction. Rechecked the live BEA release September 30 at 14:05:56 UTC; relevant figures unchanged. Avoided exact-equality wording for rounded monthly changes.
review.voice: 58 words; new-report impact first, agency and Wednesday in the second sentence, self-contained progression. Preserve whole-sentence phrasing and measured articulation; no inserted reading silence.
review.visuals: Mechanism and chart follow narration in reading order. Current inflation appears left before the Fed goal on the right. Chart starts at zero. Preserve reading time through picture holds, not extra narration pauses.
